jobs.title: Sr. Total Rewards Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi! I’m Rachel and I lead People Operations here at Ashby. I recently joined and I’m excited that we're expanding our team! The People Operations Team provides support to Ashby employees through the development and implementation of programs, policies, and services that contribute to a productive and inclusive working environment. We ensure that the work we do aligns with our Operating Principles and strengthens the environment we're building at Ashby. Our approach is to do things differently – we prioritize what truly fits our team and enhances how we work together. By embracing creativity and customization, we aim to create a people-first culture that drives both individual and organizational success.

We review all applications, and there isn’t a benefit to applying quickly. Take your time, look at the application questions and please submit before the application deadline! We aren’t able to take calls outside of the interview process, so reaching out to the team won’t push your application forward.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Total Rewards leader to build and own Ashby’s total rewards function through our next phase of growth.

This is a builder’s role. Some of the foundation is in place; a lot of it isn’t. You’ll set the philosophy, design the frameworks, build the infrastructure, and run the work day to day. It’s a chance to shape how a company rewards its people rather than administer decisions someone else made.

It’s also unusually analytical, and unusually creative. Ashby’s Total Rewards philosophy is principled and intentionally not one-size-fits-all: approaches vary by function, because different parts of the business compete in different talent markets. Total Rewards partners closely with leadership to provide the structure, documentation, guidance, and governance that keep those approaches equitable, competitive, and scalable. The upshot is that the most interesting problems here don’t have off-the-shelf answers. How do you price a role that survey data doesn’t cover? How do you keep a flexible system fair and explainable? How do you tell, early, that one talent market has moved while the others haven’t? You’ll need real fluency with data, the discipline to structure a problem before you solve it, and the confidence to invent the model when no model exists.

A lot of this work looks less like administering a program and more like a well-run strategy engagement: frame the question, get the data, build the model, pressure-test the answer, and bring leaders a recommendation with the tradeoffs made explicit. The difference is that here you also go implement it.

You’ll partner closely with People Ops, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Legal, and functional leaders to design programs that support how Ashby attracts, retains, and rewards exceptional people — building a more scalable approach while preserving the flexibility each part of the business needs.

We’re looking for someone who has built and scaled Total Rewards in high-growth, VC-backed SaaS companies and is energized by all three of philosophy, systems, and execution — someone who would rather go build the analysis than wait for it.

This role starts as an individual contributor and is expected to grow into people management as the function scales.

You'll be responsible for

Building Ashby’s compensation infrastructure

Bands, leveling alignment, market positioning, review cadences, benchmarking methodology, and clear guidance for offers, promotions, refreshers, and market adjustments — globally, and in partnership with founders, executives, and functional leaders. Some areas are mature; others are still forming. You’ll bring structure to the ambiguity with frameworks that are principled, practical, and hold up under scrutiny. You will be responsible for helping leaders reason through tradeoffs, bringing them a clear recommendation and the logic behind it, and documenting the non-standard rather than handing anyone a rule book.

Reading the market and helping Ashby adapt quickly

Combine market data, internal data, and outside signals to allow us to respond quickly and at scale when conditions change. Build the mechanisms that catch market movement across the whole company, not just the functions with the loudest signals: find the gaps in survey coverage, spot which teams are repricing faster than others, form a view on why, and turn what you see into a recommendation.

Owning Total Rewards strategy end-to-end

Compensation, equity, benefits, and perks. With founders and company leaders, define the philosophy, principles, and long-term direction for how we reward people globally. Evaluate our programs continuously and make recommendations that balance market competitiveness, internal equity, business needs, and long-term sustainability — framed the way a good strategy memo is framed: the options, the tradeoffs, and where you land.

Leading benefits strategy and administration

Own global benefits end to end: strategy, selection, renewals, plan design, competitiveness assessment, broker and vendor management, and the systems and processes behind a strong employee experience.

Leading equity program infrastructure

Partner with Finance and company leadership to bring structure, consistency, and scalability to equity practices, support program administration, and help employees understand how equity fits within the broader Total Rewards picture.

Building scalable systems and operations

Improve the systems, workflows, documentation, and operational processes behind Total Rewards. You will work in tools like CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp. You will use automation, AI, and good operational design to get roles to market quickly, support pay decisions efficiently, and keep the underlying data trustworthy.

Acting as a trusted cross-functional partner

You’re the subject matter expert for Total Rewards at Ashby. You’ll help leaders navigate rewards decisions with sound judgment, fairness, and clarity — and make complicated questions land simply in front of founders and executives.

Preparing the function to scale

You begin as a hands-on functional owner, but you’ll build with future scale in mind by establishing the documentation, operating rhythms, standards, and decision-making frameworks the function will need as it grows, and flagging the organizational needs ahead.

You could be a great fit if

  • You bring several years of progressive Total Rewards experience, including meaningful ownership of compensation, benefits, and equity programs in high-growth organizations and you’ve built compensation infrastructure from the ground up.

  • You bring an analytical first mindset. You build the model, pressure-test your own numbers, and would rather run the analysis yourself than wait for someone else to.

  • You’re a structured thinker. You take a messy question, break it into the parts that matter, form a hypothesis, and test it — and you can walk someone through your reasoning without losing them.

  • You’re a creative problem solver in the comp space. When benchmarks are thin or the role is new, you reason from first principles and design the approach that fits the problem and not the one you used last time.

  • You’re comfortable where some principles are centralized and other elements are tailored by function, and you can keep that flexibility equitable and explainable.

  • You’ve built and scaled compensation frameworks and benefits programs for globally distributed organizations, ideally through periods of significant growth.

  • You can support leaders with different needs and viewpoints while holding the line on trust, consistency, and decision quality.

  • You’re highly effective at both strategy and execution, and comfortable being the primary owner of the work day to day.

  • You’re an exceptional communicator who can make complex Total Rewards topics land with any audience and can show the reasoning behind a number, not just the number. You’re comfortable putting a recommendation in front of founders and defending it.

  • You’re detail-oriented and operationally strong, always looking for ways to improve systems, processes, and program quality.

  • You’ve led or managed others, or you’re excited to build and eventually scale a Total Rewards team.

Bonus points if you have

  • Experience building and scaling global compensation and benefits programs across multiple regions and employment models.

  • Experience using automation, AI, and technology to make Total Rewards operations faster, more accurate, and more scalable.

  • Strong modeling and data skills beyond the standard toolkit including advanced spreadsheet work, SQL, Python, or BI tools.

  • A background that blends Total Rewards with strategy consulting, corporate finance or FP&A, or people analytics. We value people who have been trained to structure and solve ambiguous problems, wherever they learned to do it.

  • Experience with tools such as CandorIQ, Pave, and OpenComp.

This role may not be a fit if

  • You want to bring your own Total Rewards playbook and install it at Ashby, rather than reimagine and evolve what’s already been started.

  • You prefer operating inside highly standardized programs to building and adapting them in a more flexible environment.

  • You’re less interested in the hands-on work of running the function — including doing the analysis yourself.

  • You reach for the benchmark before the reasoning, or you need rigid rules to make a call.

  • You’d rather present the data than the recommendation.

  • You’re uncomfortable making decisions in ambiguity or helping leaders through nuanced compensation questions.

  • Most of your experience is in mature organizations with established programs, processes, and teams, without having had to build infrastructure through growth and change.

  • Recruiter Screen with Talent Acquisition Team - 30 minutes

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 45 minutes

  • Take Home Assignment

    • Followed by 1 hour live session to discuss

  • Virtual Onsite - 2.5-3 hours

  • Final Round with CEO - 30 minutes

We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

jobs.title: Strategic Customer Success Manager - Americas
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About this Role

Hi, I’m Loren, the Head of Strategic Customer Success here at Ashby. My team is dedicated to building deep, consultative partnerships within the Enterprise space.

Our Customer Success Team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional upmarket customer experience across the Enterprise Segment. We’re thrilled to be hiring our next Strategic CSM as we continue to grow the team.

In this role, you'll guide Ashby's biggest customers - focusing on improved product adoption and increased customer health. You will shape how we serve customers ranging from high growth organizations to public companies.

Ashby is designed to be powerful and flexible, allowing users to adjust it to their needs. This means that there is a lot to learn. You will become a product and domain expert in order to enable our customers to make the best use of Ashby to drive hiring excellence.

Role Requirements:

  • You have a strong track record of customer success experience in B2B SaaS (at least five years), supporting the implementation and adoption of complex technologies through the customer journey.

  • You’re comfortable managing a book of ~20 strategic customers, exceeding $2m in total ARR. You enjoy multi-threading, developing relationships across a broad set of stakeholders while supporting existing teams to drive adoption and retention.

  • You have experience working closely with cross-functional stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Operations.

  • You love becoming a product and industry expert. You create ‘Ah ha!’ moments by tailoring configuration, driving product adoption, and crafting training to address a customer’s specific challenges so they achieve their intended business outcomes.

  • You’ve worked with technically complex products and show a strong curiosity to explore details and understand how things work.

You Should Apply If:

  • 📣 You communicate with precision and clarity. You can take something complex (like a multi-layered report or a nuanced workflow) and explain it simply and confidently.

  • 🎧 You are a listener first. You seek to understand what customers actually need and then advocate for them internally to shape how Ashby evolves for enterprise use cases.

  • ⚙️You thrive in complexity. Ashby is powerful and highly configurable; you’re energized by learning a product with depth, and you can translate that knowledge into creative solutions for your customers.

  • 🧑‍🏫 You’re excited to help shape a new segment. Our Strategic customer motion is still evolving; you’ll be iterating on playbooks, helping us learn what works, and turning those learnings into repeatable processes for the team.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You send crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates.

  • 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data.

  • 👥You may have been a recruiter, hiring manager, or interviewer before. That experience helps you quickly connect Ashby’s workflows to real-world hiring problems (though it’s not required).

Why you shouldn’t apply:

  • You prefer managing a broad, high-volume book of business (if so, see our Mid-Market or Startup roles).

  • You're interested in managing customer accounts with infrequent and well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work).

  • You shine as an exclusively commercial CSM, motivated by variable compensation. While our team's north star metric is revenue retention, we focus on adoption and engagement as leading indicators. For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a remarkable team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay, aligning with our strategy to hire product-oriented CSMs rather than adhering to the conventional Account Manager model.

  • You’re afraid of rolling up your sleeves. If the idea of getting in the weeds with a customer about the nuance between a time in process report and a time to hire report feels too granular, or project managing a workflow change for offer approvals isn’t interesting, this job isn’t going to be for you.

About Ashby

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better.

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

  • Intro Call with Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 45 Minutes

  • Mock Customer Call - 45 Minutes

  • Final Round - 1 hour

    • Rather than a traditional panel interview with a large group, we structure our panel into two focused conversations. This gives you the opportunity to meet with multiple team members in a more conversational setting centered on specific topics, instead of a formal Q&A. You'll discuss how you approach problem solving, dive into a product complexity exercise, then wrap up with a quick closing call with the hiring manager.

Benefits

  • You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. We also offer a 3% 401k match.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I’m Rosalia, and I look after our Product Marketing team at Ashby. I started my career in Product Marketing and helped build the Sales Enablement function at HubSpot during its journey from startup to IPO. Since then, I've worked across RevOps and Customer Marketing at Procore and Meta, partnering with incredible teams to bring differentiated products to market. I first heard of Ashby through our Head of Content, Anum, with whom I'd spent those early days at HubSpot, and was inspired by the level of thoughtfulness and operating principles I saw and read about. I joined Ashby in April of 2024 to lead Product Marketing, thrilled to build something meaningful with people I admire, and to help shape the future of hiring in a way that's thoughtful, effective, and human.

We're a small team with high standards and mutual respect for our teammates and community. The way we do Product Marketing at Ashby reflects that, all with a good dose of fun 🎉. We value clarity over cleverness, lean into autonomy, and treat writing well and first-principles thinking as core parts of the job. We avoid jargon, favor plain English, and focus on helping customers and prospects genuinely understand what our product does and how it can help them.

What we’re looking for

We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own our Enterprise narrative, content and enable our go-to-market teams with clarity and confidence.

This includes the messaging, content, and sales support that helps us win and grow our largest, most complex customers. This role is about deeply understanding what it takes to sell and support Ashby at the Enterprise level: longer sales cycles, more sophisticated buying committees, and a much wider set of stakeholders (Finance, Legal, Analysts, Heads of Talent, RecOps, and more).

You'll partner closely with our Director of Product Marketing to make sure Enterprise messaging ladders up to Ashby's overarching company narrative, while you go deep on what makes that narrative land specifically with Enterprise and upper mid-market buyers. You will synthesize inputs from customer research, product direction, market dynamics, and company vision into clear, compelling narratives that scale across the segment.

You’ll work hand-in-hand with Solutions Engineers and Sales Leaders to drive success within the segment, as well as collaborate with other marketing teams such as our Content & Community, Demand Gen, Events and Partnerships, to influence campaigns for the Enterprise segment.

This role is a great fit for someone who loves to problem-solve through complexity, enjoys working with sophisticated buyers, and wants to own a full segment end-to-end.

Your Background

There's no perfect path into this role. We're open to a variety of backgrounds, including:

  • Product Marketing

  • Sales Enablement

  • Competitive Intelligence

  • Solutions Consulting or Sales Engineering

What You’ll Do

Own Enterprise segment narrative development

  • Conduct deep research and develop messaging for the full Enterprise buying committee: Finance, Legal, Analysts, Heads of Talent, RecOps, and other stakeholders that don't show up the same way in smaller segments.

  • Translate Ashby's company-level narrative into a story that resonates with Enterprise and upper mid-market buyers.

  • Maintain the Enterprise messaging framework that empowers Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success to communicate, sell and service Ashby’s differentiation with confidence.

Be a strategic partner to Enterprise sales

  • Partner deeply with Sales Leadership and Solutions Engineering to identify opportunities within the segment

  • Develop Enterprise-specific enablement and build campaigns and materials that support the Enterprise sales process.

  • Act as the source of truth and connective tissue between Marketing, CS, and Sales on how to speak to the Enterprise buyer, overall messaging and collateral

  • Deliver well-crafted trainings to sales in collaboration with other sales-supporting teams to move forward audience positioning and other key initiatives.

Develop Enterprise-specific content

  • Own the content and collateral that's unique to Enterprise: case studies, decks, one-pagers, and campaigns, including 1-1 and 1-to-few ABM built for this buyer set.

  • Support TCO reports and ROI content that help Enterprise buyers and champions justify Ashby internally.

  • Make sure CS, Sales, and Marketing are aligned and working from the same Enterprise messaging.

Examples of Projects You'll Work On

  • Support Enterprise ABM initiatives: Support enterprise messaging for the marketing ABM program with the content, and compelling creative campaigns that support 1-1 and 1-to-few messaging.

  • Analyst Relations Briefs: Partnering with Analyst Relations to prepare and brief analysts and press on Ashby’s offerings.

  • Sales Leadership Strategic Initiatives: Work with Sales Leadership to translate big ideas and top company priorities into actionable assets, initiatives and roll outs that the Sales Team can use to drive deals forward.

  • Enterprise buying committee messaging: Build out messaging tailored to secondary Enterprise stakeholders (Legal, Analysts, RecOps) who influence but don't lead the buying process.

  • Enterprise sales deck refresh: Partner with Sales leadership to refresh the core Enterprise pitch as our narrative evolves.

  • Cross-functional alignment: Make sure CS, Sales, and Marketing are aligned and using the same Enterprise messaging as new campaigns roll out.

You Might Be a Fit If You ...

  • Love the complexity of Enterprise buying: multiple stakeholders, longer cycles, higher stakes.

  • Are a confident writer who can flex a company narrative to resonate with a more sophisticated, skeptical buyer.

  • Are comfortable owning your own copy and collaborating with design to produce polished, Enterprise-grade assets.

  • Like partnering closely with Sales and being in the room for their biggest deals.

You Might Not Be a Fit If ...

  • You are drained by ambiguity or unsolved problems.

  • You don't love the enablement aspects of product marketing.

  • You'd rather work on message development in the abstract than get into the weeds of a specific deal or buyer.

  • You are not a confident writer and storyteller.

Interview Process

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

  • 30 min: Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

  • 45 min: Interview with Hiring Manager (Rosalia)

  • 30 min: Interview with Marketing

  • Assignment

  • Final Round with key stakeholders

Benefits

  • You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

  • Competitive compensation is offered.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. We hope that excites you enough to apply

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. jobs.title: Implementation Consultant - Americas
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Implementation Consultant - Americas

Hi! I’m Morgan, the Manager of Strategic Implementations here at Ashby. Our customers are at the center of everything we do, and that’s especially true during implementation. We take pride in being responsive, collaborative partners who focus not just on delivery, but on thoughtful execution.

I’m thrilled to be expanding our implementation motion by hiring an Implementation Consultant. As part of our growing Professional Services team within Ashby’s Customer Success organization, you’ll play a critical part in helping customers bridge the gap between potential and actual value.

About this role:

As our Implementation Consultant, you will own execution of the technical configuration for a defined set of new Ashby customers. During these implementations, you will partner closely with an Implementation Specialist to confirm customer requirements before leading the tailored configuration of native platform functionality. As initial configuration concludes, you will define and carry out a testing plan ahead of go-live. You will also document final configuration choices made to ensure visibility and allow for ongoing optimization post-launch.

As we scale, we’re investing in more specialized implementation roles to ensure customers get to value quickly. This role is ideal for someone earlier in their implementation or customer-facing career who is excited to learn, grow, and develop deep expertise in a complex product. You’ll work with increasing independence over time with support from more senior Implementation Specialists and cross-functional partners. This role is designed as a pathway into the more senior Implementation Specialist role over time.

Role requirements:

  • Complex SaaS Implementation & Project Management: You have deep experience contributing to or owning implementation projects for complex SaaS products (actioning a defined project plan, communicating and aligning with stakeholders on progress, and ultimately delivering results in accordance with the agreed upon expectations). You feel comfortable independently owning your domain, as well as keeping customers accountable to theirs. You work effectively in a remote-first setting, with the ability to travel as needed (<5%) for strategic customer engagements.

  • Customer Centricity: You are adept at understanding enterprise customer needs and tailoring implementation configurations to meet their specific requirements. You build strong customer relationships by maintaining high levels of engagement and communication. You serve as the customer’s proactive guide and advocate related to technical configuration, balancing empathy and practicality throughout the implementation. Bonus points if you have prior familiarity with Talent Acquisition teams and processes.

  • Technical Proficiency: You have a solid understanding of a complex product (ideally Ashby) and its technical intricacies. You are technically curious and creative.

  • Critical Thinking & Solutions Orientation: You proactively address thematic customer opportunities and improve our processes accordingly. You don’t rely on ‘I’ve seen this done,’ but instead think critically to solve problems. You anticipate how configuration decisions might impact customer goals, ask questions to validate options, and pair your recommendations with risk mitigation tactics.

  • Best Practices & Recommendations: You take pride in advising customers on best practices specific to their usage of software to ensure optimal value.

  • Change Management: You are experienced in navigating change management processes and helping customers adapt to new systems and a refreshed approach.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration and Communication: You effectively partner with cross-functional stakeholders across Customer Success, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations to align and define progress. You proactively communicate progress and risks with internal and external stakeholders.

You could be a great fit if:

  • 🙋You strike the balance between collaborative teamwork with a strong ability to execute independently on a defined plan.

  • 📣 You demonstrate clear communication. You ask clarifying questions with precision and can distill complex concepts into simple themes.

  • 🎧 You are a great listener. You read between the lines of what customers share in order to identify core concepts, which allows you to surface the right tailored recommendations. You see your role as the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our offerings continue to evolve in accordance with customer needs.

  • 📈 You are a problem solver. You thrive at solving complex challenges with innovative, scalable solutions.

  • ⚡️You know process matters. You are eager to improve processes and workflows to enhance efficiency and efficacy.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail-oriented and technically proficient. You take pride in internal operations.

  • 📊 You are data-driven. You use metrics and analytics to inform decisions and measure success.

  • 🌍 You are adaptable. You can navigate changes in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • 🧑‍🏫 You are eager to make an impact and grow. You understand the critical role you play in a customer’s success, and seize opportunities to expand your impact for customers and the team.

You might not be a great fit if:

  • You are uninterested in customer-facing work that blends technical, operational, and interpersonal skills.

  • You are uncomfortable learning a complex product and adapting as it evolves.

  • You prefer roles that are purely strategic without hands-on execution.

Our philosophy:

Here are a few key points that should give you a sense of what it’s like to work with us:

  • We invest heavily in building best-in-class products, believing that great products make customer success easier and more meaningful.

  • We value deep expertise and thoughtful problem-solving in every customer interaction.

  • We believe small, highly capable teams outperform large teams — and we hire, support, and compensate accordingly.

  • We value ownership, principled thinking, and clear communication, regardless of tenure or level.

The Interview

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety:

  • 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team

  • 45 min - Interview with Manager of Strategic Implementations (Hiring Manager)

  • Take Home Exercise

  • 30 min - Take Home Deep Dive Interview with 2 Strategic Implementation Specialists

  • Final Round:

    • 30 min - Cross-functional collaboration with Head of Professional Services

    • 30 min - Product Complexity with VP of Customer Success

    • 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Data Analytics Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About this Role

👋 Hi, I’m Kevin. I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional.

You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem.

The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company.

Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers.

  1. Can you identify and hire talented people?

    We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others?

  2. Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work?

    Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate.

  3. Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization?

    Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists.

  4. Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI?

    AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy.

These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members.


Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager

To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today.

Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company.

As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well.

Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply

At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well.

You could be a strong fit if you:

  • Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome.

  • Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion.

  • Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work.

  • Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking.

  • Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive - Germany
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Join Sales at Ashby

Sales at Ashby is a unique opportunity to sell a product customers genuinely love during an AI-fueled market expansion. Over 5,000 companies rely on Ashby, including OpenAI, Bolt, Statista, Neura Robotics and Monday.com, and our business is durably growing faster than 100% year-over-year. We’re well funded, and on a path to profitability. That's exceptionally rare for a company at our scale, and puts us in the top 10% of benchmarks.

Nearly 1 in 3 of Ashby’s globally distributed team call Europe home! We’ve landed over 1000 customers in EMEA representing ~23% of our global revenue base, with well over 100 in the DACH region, clear evidence of strong product-market fit. We’re doubling down our investment in the region with in-market GTM, CS and Support resources. EU Data Residency and product localisation are committed and coming soon. We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to help modern teams move beyond legacy recruiting software.

Ashby replaces 3-5 tools in a consolidation & efficiency play that’s equally loved by recruiters and CFOs. We’re known as a clear AI-leader in the recruiting space. We are rapidly extending from a best-in-class recruiting product toward a multi-product platform, expanding upmarket, into new industries, and internationally. For sales reps, that means a large market full of legacy tools, and a product portfolio that creates room for both new business and expansion. This is a chance to participate in how a category-defining company wins in its next phase of growth.

We are equally intentional about how we build the business. We have established a remote-first, high-performing sales organization that rewards learning and accountability. We use data to set achievable quotas, and reward sustained impact with competitive compensation and meaningful upside. We prioritize coaching and career development, with AEs advancing to Enterprise & Leadership roles in just a few years — 38% of the team who have been here more than a year have been promoted or taken on a new role!

You will work with people who care about craft, customer outcomes, and winning together—without sacrificing the trust, autonomy, and balance required to do your best work over the long term. Don’t just take my word for it, see what the team has to say about working here.

About this Role

TA tools in the Enterprise represent a huge market opportunity, a $1B+ TAM, and the incumbents are legacy players. We are displacing a collection of tools (ATS, Sourcing & CRM, Scheduling, Analytics, Offers & Approvals) with a consolidated talent suite. This is a proven playbook that Workday used to win the HCM market as customers realize value in a multitude of ways.

We are seeking a German-fluent and Germany-based Enterprise Account Executive to help us win Enterprise (1,000+ employees) accounts by managing the full sales cycle from pipeline generation through to closed-won.

In this role, you'll focus on new logo acquisition. Our emphasis is on your ability to excel in the areas listed below and your appetite for continuous growth & improvement.

You could be a great fit if:

  • 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms.

  • 💰 You have strong track record in Enterprise SaaS sales, having closed many $100k sales, and overachieved $1M+ quotas consistently. You have won competitive rip-and-replace opportunities of core/platform technologies.

  • 🎯 You are proactive in identifying and pursuing new business opportunities, and comfortable sourcing >50% of your own pipeline. You're both resourceful and innovative in finding new business opportunities.

  • 💻 You can confidently deliver micro-demos before engaging your SE partners. You can't imagine not being fluent in the product you sell.

  • 🎧 You are highly skilled at discovery. You believe in preparation to establish a point of view, and through discovery validate or refine your perspective to identify a project's business drivers aligned to executive priorities.

  • 🤝 You have strong business acumen. You quickly connect the dots between technical problems and their downstream business impacts. You craft compelling business cases with this context.

  • ⚔️ You're adept at competitive or evangelical selling in new or established markets.

  • 🏔️ You skillfully guide prospects through the evaluation—engaging the right stakeholders at the right time to create consensus for a strategic technology decision.

  • 🤓 You enjoy becoming an expert and tailoring discussions to address each prospect’s unique challenges.

  • ⚡️ Your peers describe you as action-oriented and persistent. You're always on the leaderboard for outbound effort and pipeline created.

  • 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You write and send crisp follow-up emails, on time. You also take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates. (We use HubSpot, Gong, Chili Piper and Apollo.)

  • ✈️ You are willing to travel at least 25% of the time for customer engagements and events.

Requirements:

  • 🤝 You have 5+ years of full-cycle closing experience and have closed many >$100,000 ACV opportunities

  • 📢 You have experience selling complex platform technologies in a sales-led GTM motion

  • 📈 You are a new business hunter and are confident in your abilities to self-source >50% of your own pipeline

  • 🌍 You have sold to multiple regions within EMEA and have strong written and verbal fluency in both English and German

  • 🇩🇪 You are based in Germany

Bonus Points:

  • 🤝 You have experience selling to Talent or People leaders

You shouldn't apply if:

  • 💼 You're more of a relationship builder who focuses on selling into the install base and aren't excited about a new business focused role.

  • 🎯 You expect Marketing or BDRs to source all of your pipeline for you. This is a hunting role.

  • 💻 You believe that "tech stuff" is the SE's job. Our AEs all develop product acumen while SEs are a partner in our team selling motion.

  • 📊 You prefer to run established playbooks in well defined environments. This role requires creativity and a growth mindset.

  • 🐺 You're a lone wolf. You prefer to go it alone in your pursuit of new business. We believe in a team-selling sales model.

Interview Process

Our interview process is thorough — we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

  • Intro Call (30 min) - You'll meet with a Recruiter to discuss your fit for the role and address questions about our market and solution.

  • Written Exercise - You'll complete a short take home assignment to showcase your outbound muscle.

  • Experience Deep Dive (60 min) - You'll walk the Hiring Manager [Casper Bergmans] through your career journey in some detail to highlight your experience, achievements, and points of learning to understand how you've developed into the professional you are today.

  • Challenge Interview (90 min) - This will be made up of two parts:

    • Discovery and Demo Role Play (60 min)

    • Deal Strategy Discussion (30 min)

Benefits

  • Compelling benefits offerings, location dependent

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

We're in the talent acquisition software business. We run the end-to-end hiring process through our own platform, and ensure a level playing field for all candidates. Reaching out to hiring managers or recruiters directly won't improve your odds of success. Please focus your energy on the quality of your application.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: GTM Systems Analyst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role

Ashby's GTM engine runs on a set of interconnected systems. Keeping them accurate, efficient, and trusted is the foundation everything else is built on. As our GTM Systems Analyst, you'll own the daily maintenance and configuration of technical layer that powers our Go-to-Market organization: the CRM configurations, integration architecture, and data quality practices that let our Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams move fast with confidence.

This role sits within Revenue Operations, the horizontal function that makes the entire GTM system work. You'll be embedded in daily operations (triaging issues, implementing new tooling, and translating business requirements into scalable configurations) while also contributing to longer-term systems strategy as we move up-market and expand our product suite.

Why this role matters now

We're in an active expansion phase: new products, new segments, new GTM motions. Our systems need to keep pace. The person in this role will shape how we build the technical foundation for the next chapter of Ashby's growth.

What You'll Do

  • System Administration: Own the day-to-day health of our core GTM platforms. You'll manage configuration, user permissions, custom objects, and workflow automation across our CRM stack — making sure the systems actually reflect how our teams work, not just how they were set up two years ago.

  • Integration Support: Maintain clean data flows across our GTM toolset ( including intent data, conversation intelligence, and sales engagement platforms). You'll be the person who knows how signals travel between systems and why, and who makes sure they're flowing reliably.

  • Data Governance: Enforce standards for data quality, deduplication, and field taxonomy. Revenue reporting and forecasting are only as good as the data underneath them, along with our GTM Engineers and our System Architect, you'll build the infrastructure of trust that makes those outputs credible.

  • Stakeholder Support: Be the go-to technical partner for frontline GTM teams. You'll triage issues, gather business requirements, and deliver solutions that scale. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical partners and know when to say "that requires a bigger conversation" rather than patching around a root cause.

  • Tooling Evaluation: Help evaluate new GTM tech and AI tools as our needs evolve. You'll assess how new tools will integrate with our existing systems, support contract renewals, and support implementation of emerging solutions, with a practical bias toward what will actually get adopted and maintained.

What We're Looking For

  • Advanced proficiency in CRM administration: Salesforce Administrator or HubSpot Administrator certification strongly preferred

  • Experience connecting marketing automation, CRM, and revenue intelligence tools (e.g., 6sense, Gong, Outreach, Gainsight)

  • Ability to translate abstract business goals into documented, scalable technical configurations

  • Strong analytical skills: you can diagnose data discrepancies, form a hypothesis, and present findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Instinctive troubleshooter: you don't wait for a problem to be fully described before you start hypothesizing

  • Clear written communicator; we're a remote-first company and documentation is how work gets shared

  • 2–4 years in a RevOps, Marketing Ops, or Sales Ops systems role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with SQL or data warehouse querying (Snowflake, BigQuery) for ad hoc analysis

  • Experience with AI-assisted workflow automation or prompt-based tooling in a GTM context

  • Exposure to multi-product or multi-segment GTM motions

This role may not be a fit if:

  • You have used CRM systems extensively, but have not owned CRM administration work directly. Hubspot is our current CRM.

  • You prefer strategy and architecture work over hands-on systems ownership.

  • You do your best work when requirements are fully specified, rather than when you need to diagnose ambiguous issues and triage incoming requests.

  • You are looking for a role focused on one GTM function, rather than broad partnership across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

Interview process

  1. Recruiter Screen

  2. Hiring Manager Interview

  3. Challenge Interview

  4. Final Round with multiple key stakeholders

At Ashby, we’re building the future of enterprise software—starting with a suite of products that empower talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers to drive better hiring outcomes with data-informed strategies. We're backed by Y Combinator and top-tier investors like Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. Our customers include global leaders like Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, and Notion.

We’re growing fast—over 100% year-over-year in revenue and we’ve only just scratched the surface of a massive market opportunity. This is your chance to get in early and help shape a category-defining company.

Benefits

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

jobs.title: Customer Education Program Manager, Live Learning
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Hi, I'm Jace Talamantes. I founded Ashby's Customer Education function in 2025 and now lead the team. I am excited to be hiring a Customer Education Program Manager, Live Learning!

Our team is built on a simple belief: Ashby Academy should feel like every customer's personal CSM. Regardless of tier or team size, every Ashby customer deserves content that meets them where they are — practical, accurate, and genuinely useful. That standard shapes everything we build, and it's what's driven the development of our growing Academy courses, webinar program, and playbook library. We have ambitions to expand both the depth of our content and the formats we deliver it in, and this hire is a meaningful part of getting there.

As our first dedicated live-learning hire, you’ll help define what this program becomes and build the practices that make it work. Our Startup Customer Success and Recruiting Operations Consulting teams already run live sessions that customers value. You’ll lead how those experiences should come together, bring a point of view on where we should invest next, and define what great live learning at Ashby should feel like.

This role needs both vision and execution. You’ll shape the direction and stay close to the work: planning the calendar, simplifying registration, developing a workshop with an expert, coaching presenters, and hosting selected sessions yourself. You should be as interested in getting next week’s session right as you are in imagining what the program could become over the next year.

You’ll report to me and partner with Customer Success, Customer Education, and Marketing. There’s a foundation to build on and people to partner with, alongside plenty of room to set direction and drive the work. If you enjoy forming a point of view, turning it into something practical, and improving it as you learn, there’s a lot to make your own here.

What you’ll do at Ashby

  • Own the Customer Success live-learning program, bringing existing programs together under a shared calendar, planning process, and consistent customer experience. Establish a clear process for evaluating, prioritizing, and developing new ideas.

  • Make sessions easier to run. Own registration, reminders, session setup, presenter preparation, live production, surveys, follow-up, and recording handoffs. Build reusable templates and clear operating practices that reduce repeated work.

  • Design learning around customer needs. Partner with presenters and Customer Education Program Managers to define the audience, intended outcome, format, and supporting resources. Develop session outlines, exercises, facilitator guides, and other materials that help customers apply what they learn.

  • Help experts become effective presenters. Define what a high-quality session looks like, run rehearsals, coach presenters, and improve how sessions handle questions, participation, pacing, and mixed experience levels.

  • Host and facilitate selected sessions. Lead or co-facilitate learning where it serves the program, moderate questions and activities, model effective teaching, and help test new formats. Build a program that supports multiple presenters rather than depending on you to teach every session.

  • Own the live-learning recording library. Make useful sessions easy to find and learn from after the live event. Decide what to publish, how to organize it, and when to refresh or retire it. Partner with Academy operations on publishing and with presenters and CEPMs on accuracy, supporting resources, and opportunities to turn sessions into other learning formats.

  • Make sessions easy to discover and join. Work with Marketing on the website experience, audience communications, packaging, and connections to broader programs. Give customers a clear way to find the right session and their next learning step.

  • Measure and improve the program. Track registration, attendance, engagement, learner feedback, and operational effort. Define the product behavior each program is intended to support and work with partners to assess whether customers take action.

  • Expand deliberately. Use customer needs and program evidence to recommend additional audiences and formats, including onboarding sessions, RecOps clinics, applied workshops, and customer spotlights.

Our teams currently run roughly two to three sessions each week. Your initial priority is to establish reliable delivery of the existing program. You’ll work with your manager to prioritize improvements and expand formats, balancing customer needs with presenter availability and operational capacity.

How you’ll work with other teams

  • Startup CSMs and RecOps consultants will continue to lead the subject-matter content and delivery for their audiences. You’ll partner with them on learning design, preparation, and quality while owning the overall program and its operations.

  • You’ll work together with Customer Education Program Managers to decide where live learning fits and how it connects with existing courses, playbooks, and release education.

  • Marketing will partner on website presence, promotion, packaging, and broader program alignment. Operations and systems partners will support platform setup and integrations. You’ll define program requirements and work with those partners to improve workflows.

  • This role focuses on scalable customer learning. Individual customer training and consulting engagements remain with the teams responsible for those services.

Examples of work you might own

  • Bring Startup and RecOps sessions into one coordinated calendar with a consistent registration and follow-up experience.

  • Turn a presentation-heavy session into a workshop where customers practice a workflow and receive feedback.

  • Create a presenter kit with an outline, rehearsal checklist, production plan, and guidance for handling questions.

  • Work with Marketing and Event Ops to simplify webinar setup and connect registration and attendance data with our reporting.

  • Package a useful session into a recording, a short practical resource, and a clear next step in Academy.

  • Review a series with strong attendance but limited follow-through and recommend what to change before running it again.

You may be a great fit if:

  • You’ve owned recurring live education or a comparable customer-facing program and can show how you made it more useful, reliable, or scalable.

  • You come from customer education, product training, customer success, enablement, learning design, or webinar program management. What matters most is evidence that you can combine strong operational ownership with thoughtful teaching and a strong understanding of customer needs.

  • You own recurring work reliably. You can manage a calendar, multiple contributors, deadlines, and dependencies while keeping the customer experience consistent.

  • You’ve helped people learn something complex. You can explain clearly, use practical examples, and check whether someone can apply what you taught.

  • You’re comfortable facilitating live. You can guide participation, respond to questions, adjust your approach, and keep a session useful when something unexpected happens.

  • You help other people teach effectively. You can give specific, constructive feedback and help an expert turn deep knowledge into an accessible learning experience.

  • You learn products firsthand. You explore workflows, use documentation, test your understanding, and know when expert validation is needed. Prior Ashby experience is helpful, but not required.

  • You’re comfortable with the operational details. You’ve worked with webinar or virtual-learning platforms and understand registration, communications, recordings, surveys, and reporting. Experience with HubSpot or a comparable system is useful.

  • You bring a point of view and turn it into practice. You can assess an existing program, recommend what to keep, change, or build next, and personally drive the work with the right partners.

  • You use evidence to improve. You can use learner feedback and behavior to assess whether a session helped customers apply what they learned.

You may not be a great fit if:

  • You want to focus exclusively on presenting. A substantial part of this role is planning, production, systems, and supporting other presenters.

  • You want to focus on program strategy without staying close to delivery. This role includes hands-on setup, production, follow-up, and troubleshooting alongside improving how the program runs.

  • You measure success primarily by the number of events delivered. We care about whether the right customers participate, learn, and apply what the program teaches.

  • You need an established playbook for every decision. There is a foundation to build on, and you’ll help determine how it develops.

Interview process

We want the process to give you a clear picture of the work and give us practical evidence of how you approach it. Here's what you can expect:

  • An introductory conversation with Recruiting (30 minutes)

  • A hiring manager conversation about programs you’ve owned (45 minutes)

  • A bounded take-home exercise (one week to complete)

  • Final Round interview (two hours)

    • A discussion of your approach to the take-home exercise (45 minutes)

    • A conversation about facilitation and presenter coaching (30 minutes)

    • A cross-functional partnership conversation (30 minutes)

    • Closing questions with the myself, the Hiring Manager (15 minutes)

We’ll share the full schedule, preparation expectations, and evaluation criteria before the exercise.

About Ashby

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website: https://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. Following our Series D in 2025, we’re continuing to grow ARR at more than 100% year over year, serving over 5,000 customers, including industry leaders like Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, Reddit, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

 

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

Benefits

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

 - You’ve owned recurring live education or a comparable customer-facing program and can show how you made it more useful, reliable, or scalable.

 - You come from customer education, product training, customer success, enablement, learning design, or webinar program management. What matters most is evidence that you can combine strong operational ownership with thoughtful teaching and a strong understanding of customer needs.

 - You own recurring work reliably. You can manage a calendar, multiple contributors, deadlines, and dependencies while keeping the customer experience consistent.

 - You’ve helped people learn something complex. You can explain clearly, use practical examples, and check whether someone can apply what you taught.

 - You’re comfortable facilitating live. You can guide participation, respond to questions, adjust your approach, and keep a session useful when something unexpected happens.

 - You help other people teach effectively. You can give specific, constructive feedback and help an expert turn deep knowledge into an accessible learning experience.

 - You learn products firsthand. You explore workflows, use documentation, test your understanding, and know when expert validation is needed. Prior Ashby experience is helpful, but not required.

 - You’re comfortable with the operational details. You’ve worked with webinar or virtual-learning platforms and understand registration, communications, recordings, surveys, and reporting. Experience with HubSpot or a comparable system is useful.

 - You bring a point of view and turn it into practice. You can assess an existing program, recommend what to keep, change, or build next, and personally drive the work with the right partners.

 - You use evidence to improve. You can use learner feedback and behavior to assess whether a session helped customers apply what they learned.




YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - You want to focus exclusively on presenting. A substantial part of this role is planning, production, systems, and supporting other presenters.

 - You want to focus on program strategy without staying close to delivery. This role includes hands-on setup, production, follow-up, and troubleshooting alongside improving how the program runs.

 - You measure success primarily by the number of events delivered. We care about whether the right customers participate, learn, and apply what the program teaches.

 - You need an established playbook for every decision. There is a foundation to build on, and you’ll help determine how it develops.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

We want the process to give you a clear picture of the work and give us practical evidence of how you approach it. Here's what you can expect:

 - An introductory conversation with Recruiting (30 minutes)

 - A hiring manager conversation about programs you’ve owned (45 minutes)

 - A bounded take-home exercise (one week to complete)

 - Final Round interview (two hours)
   
   - A discussion of your approach to the take-home exercise (45 minutes)
   
   - A conversation about facilitation and presenter coaching (30 minutes)
   
   - A cross-functional partnership conversation (30 minutes)
   
   - Closing questions with the myself, the Hiring Manager (15 minutes)

We’ll share the full schedule, preparation expectations, and evaluation criteria before the exercise.




ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website:  https://www.ashbyhq.com/%EF%BF%BC%EF%BF%BCWehttps://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. Following our Series D in 2025, we’re continuing to grow ARR at more than 100% year over year, serving over 5,000 customers, including industry leaders like Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, Reddit, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

 


ABOUT GO TO MARKET

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

 - We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-leadership-principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.




BENEFITS

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!
